general_information.Description: Objectives: The course is designed to help students develop skills of critical reading, thinking and writing in various academic topics. Through completing a number of authentic projects of reading and writing and through teacher’s guide as well as feedback, students will be able to further their skills, at an advanced level. Description Read, Think and Write 2 focuses on reading and writing in one course to help students read from a writer's viewpoint and write with a reader in mind. It is also designed to engage students in real-world, college-level projects to gain the literacy skills they need to succeed. The course provides detailed knowledge and practice of using sources effectively, avoiding plagiarism as well as writing well-crafted sentences. Teaching Methods: The teaching process includes a variety of methods, from teachers’ side: lectures, guided learning, feedback and corrections and from students’ side: discussions, idea brainstorming and writing, peer corrections and self-corrections. Assessment scheme: 1) On-going assessment - Projects 02 55% - Peer corrections 02*5%. 10% Final exam 01 35% 2) Final Result 100% 4) Completion Criteria: a) On-going assessment >0, Each component >0 b) Final Result >=5
general_information.StudentTasks: - Students must attend at least 80% of contact slots in order to be accepted to the final examination. - Student is responsible for doing all exercises and assignments given by instructor in class or at home and submit on time - Use laptops in class only for learning purposes
general_information.Tools: Tools: Foxit pdf editor Internet access https://www.mheducation.com/

learning_outcomes.CLO Details: Utilize information sources accurately and effectively following MLA and APA styles. 1.1. Evaluate whether a source is reliable to be used for academic writing/ research. 1.2. Generate in-text citations and references accurately following MLA and APA styles.
Modify essays (organization, unity, clarity, format) effectively using reader-based suggestions.
Compose well-crafted sentences (phrases, clauses, word choice, punctuation, mechanics).
Compose a precise and concise summary from a reading text.
Compose a writing paper in response to an informative text.
Compose a writing paper in response to an argumentative text.
Persuade readers with strong arguments and evidence from reliable sources.
Develop flexibility and respect in pair work.

constructive_questions.Name: HN_CQ1
constructive_questions.Details: What is a source-based essay? Give examples.

constructive_questions.Name: HN_CQ2
constructive_questions.Details: What is bias? What are common types of bias in writing? Give examples.

constructive_questions.Name: HN_CQ3
constructive_questions.Details: How to examine for authors' bias and credibility? Why?

constructive_questions.Name: HN_CQ4
constructive_questions.Details: What are sources of bias and credibility? Which is the most common? Why?

constructive_questions.Name: HN_CQ5
constructive_questions.Details: What are the types of quotations in academic writing? Give examples. When and how to use quotations? Give examples.

constructive_questions.Name: HN_CQ6
constructive_questions.Details: What are the differences between MLA and APA in-text citation styles? Give examples.

constructive_questions.Name: HN_CQ7
constructive_questions.Details: Why do writers use a reference list? Give an example of a reference list in an APA style.

constructive_questions.Name: HN_CQ8
constructive_questions.Details: What are common types of plagiarism? Why do writers avoid plagiarism?

constructive_questions.Name: HN_CQ9
constructive_questions.Details: What are organization and unity in writing? Why are they important? Give examples of essays having good organization and unity.

constructive_questions.Name: HN_CQ10
constructive_questions.Details: What are the ways to improve organization and unity in students' paragraph and essay writing?

constructive_questions.Name: HN_CQ11
constructive_questions.Details: What are awkward and vague expressions? Give examples. Why do some writers write awkward and vague expressions? How to avoid this?

constructive_questions.Name: HN_CQ12
constructive_questions.Details: What is the recursive writing process? Give examples. Why is this process used in academic writing? Is this process useful to you? Why and why not?

constructive_questions.Name: HN_CQ13
constructive_questions.Details: How to write with clarity in pronoun reference and agreement? Give examples.

constructive_questions.Name: HN_CQ14
constructive_questions.Details: What is SMART TRACS in essay editing? Give examples. Do you think it is useful? Why?

constructive_questions.Name: HN_CQ15
constructive_questions.Details: What are interesting points in the article "Understanding Generational Differences" (p. 370)? Write a detailed outline of the article.

constructive_questions.Name: HN_CQ16
constructive_questions.Details: Write your own summary for the article. Compare and contrast your summary with the sample summary (p. 374). What can you learn from the sample to improve your summary?

constructive_questions.Name: HN_CQ17
constructive_questions.Details: Is writing an outline important before writing an essay? Why? What are psychological constraints? Write an outline for the essay on "psychological constraints".

constructive_questions.Name: HN_CQ18
constructive_questions.Details: Write an essay on psychological constraints based on the outline.

constructive_questions.Name: HN_CQ19
constructive_questions.Details: Read the essay on psychological constraints (p. 397). What are the similarities and differences between your essay and this essay? What are the interesting points of the sample essay? Why?

constructive_questions.Name: HN_CQ20
constructive_questions.Details: Write an outline for the sample essay "Psychological Constraints". Write a summary based on the outline.

constructive_questions.Name: HN_CQ21
constructive_questions.Details: Do peer feedback on your friends' works. What can you learn from your friends' summaries?

constructive_questions.Name: HN_CQ22
constructive_questions.Details: Read your friends' feedback and write an improved version of your summary.

constructive_questions.Name: HN_CQ23
constructive_questions.Details: What are the important steps and notes to tell younger students about writing a good summary? Give reasons and evidence.

constructive_questions.Name: HN_CQ24
constructive_questions.Details: Choose an article related to the lesson's topics and write a summary of about 200-300 words.

constructive_questions.Name: HN_CQ25
constructive_questions.Details: What are the main text types? What are informative texts? What are the similarities and differences between an informative and an argumentative text?

constructive_questions.Name: HN_CQ26
constructive_questions.Details: What are the things that often distract you from your main focus? Why are people easily get distracted? Give evidence for your points.

constructive_questions.Name: HN_CQ27
constructive_questions.Details: Read the informative text "Driven to Distraction: Our Wired Generation (p. 406). What are the main points discussed in the text? What are the interesting points or facts from the text? Why? What are the points you agree or disagree with? Why?

constructive_questions.Name: HN_CQ28
constructive_questions.Details: Provide feedback on your peers' writings.

constructive_questions.Name: HN_CQ29
constructive_questions.Details: What are some examples of fake news? Why are some people are gullible? Give examples and evidence for your points.

constructive_questions.Name: HN_CQ30
constructive_questions.Details: Read the informative text "A Harsh Truth about Fake News: Some people are Super Gullible" (p. 410). What are the main points discussed in the text? What are the interesting points or facts from the text? Why? What are the points agree or disagree with? Why?

constructive_questions.Name: HN_CQ31
constructive_questions.Details: Provide feedback on your peers' writings.

constructive_questions.Name: HN_CQ32
constructive_questions.Details: Write an informative essay on reasons for the spread of fake news. Use 3-5 MLA in-text citations and references.

constructive_questions.Name: HN_CQ33
constructive_questions.Details: What are advantages and disadvantages of children using social media?

constructive_questions.Name: HN_CQ34
constructive_questions.Details: Read the informative text "The Bad, the Ugly, and the Good of Kids" Use of Social Media (p. 412). What are the main points discussed in the text? What are the interesting points or facts from the text? Why? What are the points you agree or disagree with? Why?

constructive_questions.Name: HN_CQ35
constructive_questions.Details: Provide feedback on your peers' writings.

constructive_questions.Name: HN_CQ36
constructive_questions.Details: Write an essay on negative and positive sides of children using social media. Use 3-5 MLA in-text citations and references.

constructive_questions.Name: HN_CQ37
constructive_questions.Details: Is news on Facebook posts credible? Why?

constructive_questions.Name: HN_CQ38
constructive_questions.Details: Read the informative text "Facebook's False Faces Undermine Its Credibility" (p. 417). What are the main points discussed in the text? What are the interesting points or facts from the text? Why?/What are the points you agree or disagree with? Why?

constructive_questions.Details: Provide feedback on your peers' writings.

constructive_questions.Name: HN_CQ40
constructive_questions.Details: Write an essay on causes and solutions for young people spending a lot of time on Facebook. Use 3-5 APA in-text citations and references.
